def: Any actor the system accounts for separately, such as a user account, a process or a service with its own credentials.
The line between what a principal can change and what it cannot; anything a decision relies on belongs outside the proposer's.
The agent in a research loop that writes candidate changes; it is the least trusted principal.
The code that runs a candidate against checks and produces the score that decides what is kept.
Raising the measured reward without doing what the designer meant, which needs only a loose score and search pressure.
The study of safety measures that still work if a capable model is deliberately trying to subvert them.
A pipeline that combines an untrusted model, a trusted model and limited human review to produce safe output.
The share of candidates whose public score is high while their private score is low or a wall was tripped, reported next to the score.
A trusted program tricked into using its own authority on behalf of an untrusted party.
A written account of assets, principals, boundaries, capabilities, attack paths, controls and residual risk.
